title: ChatGPT
summary: An LLM chat service: queue and batch requests onto GPU replicas, stream tokens back over SSE, and manage the KV cache, rate limits and conversation storage around a scarce, expensive accelerator fleet.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Users chat in conversations; responses stream token by token
Conversation history, regenerate, stop generation; file/image inputs
Plans with different models and usage limits
Time to first token < 1 s p50; steady ~30–80 tokens/s per stream

blocks.text: Details of any specific provider's internals aren't public; this follows public LLM-serving practice (vLLM, continuous batching, PagedAttention).

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Compute is the bottleneck, not the web tier. Every design choice should raise tokens per GPU per second: batching, KV cache reuse, and routing short requests to smaller models.

head: Data
Key
Store
rows: Same store; tree via parent_id (regenerations branch)
Redis counters + durable ledger for billing

blocks.caption: Web tier is cheap; the scheduler and GPU fleet are the system

items: Gateway checks auth and plan limits (tokens per minute, messages per window).
Chat service loads history, truncates/summarizes to fit the context window, applies system prompt.
Router picks model + replica pool (by load, region, prefix-cache affinity) and enqueues.
Replica runs prefill (process the prompt) then decode (one token per step), streaming tokens back through the chat service as SSE.
On completion, persist the message and usage; side effects (titles, moderation logs) async.

sections.title: Deep dive: batching and the KV cache

items: Decode is memory-bandwidth bound: one token per sequence per step. Batching many sequences per step multiplies throughput almost for free.
**Continuous batching:** sequences join and leave the batch every step, so a long reply doesn't hold short ones hostage.
**KV cache:** attention keys/values for past tokens are kept in GPU memory; it's often the limit on batch size.
**PagedAttention:** store KV cache in fixed-size blocks like virtual memory pages, cutting fragmentation and enabling sharing.
**Prefix caching:** reuse KV for shared prefixes (system prompt, earlier turns) — route a conversation back to the replica that holds its prefix.
Prefill and decode can be split onto different pools (disaggregated serving) since they stress GPUs differently.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Throughput comes from batch size; batch size is limited by KV-cache memory; so KV-cache management is the heart of LLM serving.

items: Stop button → cancel request propagates to the replica so the sequence leaves the batch immediately (saves GPU).
If the client disconnects, keep generating briefly and persist, so a refresh shows the full answer.
Backpressure: buffer tokens per stream; slow clients don't block the GPU step.
Rate limits in tokens, not just requests: a token bucket per user per model, plus org-level quotas.
Admission control: when queues exceed a target wait, shed free-tier traffic first, fall back to a smaller model, or show a 'busy' message.
Priority queues per plan; deadlines so queued requests that would exceed timeout are dropped early.
Autoscaling is slow (GPU nodes, model load minutes) — keep warm headroom and shift traffic across regions.

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Retries during overload multiply load on the scarcest resource. Use retry budgets and return 429 with Retry-After.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Client resumes / regenerates; persist partial output
Admission control, tiered priority, smaller-model fallback
Separate pools by context length, chunked prefill
Canary per region, eval gates, instant rollback
Cache recent conversation context; write async

items.text: Continuous batching + KV cache, streaming + cancel, overload.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Metrics: TTFT, tokens/s, queue wait, GPU util, cost per 1k tokens.

items.q: How do you handle a conversation longer than the context window?
items.a: Truncate oldest turns, summarize earlier history, or retrieve relevant past turns via embeddings.

items.q: How would you add tool use / browsing?
items.a: Model emits a tool call; orchestrator runs it (sandboxed), appends the result, resumes decoding.
Count input/output tokens at the replica, emit usage events to Kafka, aggregate idempotently into a ledger.
Quantization, speculative decoding, smaller models for easy prompts, prefix caching, higher batch sizes.

items: GPU time is the cost; maximize tokens/GPU/s.
Prefill then decode; decode is memory-bandwidth bound.
Continuous batching + PagedAttention KV cache.
Prefix-cache affinity routing.
SSE for token streams; cancel frees GPU.
Rate limit in tokens; shed and downgrade under load.
